question: What worker-thread count should the app give the translation engine, and does capping it fix the multi-second stalls reported in issue #60?

method.design: One llama-server per setting, started and stopped around each measurement, driven with twelve real subtitle lines after a warm-up call. Each setting measured twice: on an otherwise quiet machine, and again under a synthetic load of eight busy threads held for the duration.
method.host: Snapdragon X Elite X1E80100, 12 cores, 31.6 GB RAM
method.note: -ngl 0 is the shipped ARM64 execution policy; see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and 2026-08-05-arm64-adreno-offload-ab.json.

finding: llama.cpp's unset default was the slowest configuration tested on an idle host: 443ms median and 19.3 tok/s, against 298ms and 27.4 tok/s at six threads and 337ms and 24.8 tok/s at eight. Under load the settings separate differently - eight threads held a p90 of 377ms against six's 3814ms and the default's 22695ms. Eight was therefore chosen: it costs 39ms of idle median against the best setting and returns a tenfold better p90 on a busy machine, which is the frame a subtitle app is judged on.
counterFinding: Capping threads does not fix the tail, and the rationale originally given in issue #60 - that llama.cpp stalls at its thread barrier when a worker is descheduled - is not supported by this data. Every setting tested, including the chosen one, still produced single calls between 53 and 86 seconds under sustained load. The stalls are not a thread-count problem, so the translation slot needs its own deadline; that is implemented separately and is what actually bounds the outage.
decision: Ship --threads derived from the host core count as cores minus four, floored at four, computed in src-tauri/src/engine_launch.rs rather than pinned in the manifest, since the manifest is one embedded document shipped to every machine. A manifest that pins a thread count is honoured unchanged.
limitations: One machine, one core count. The cores-minus-four rule is extrapolated from a single 12-core measurement and is not evidence for 4-, 8- or 16-core hosts.
Twelve lines per setting, so the loaded maxima are single observations rather than a distribution.
The synthetic load is eight busy threads, which is not the shape of the reporter's real load (an installer build plus a browser plus other applications).
Measured against the server directly. Capture, OCR and overlay are not exercised, so this is not capture-to-overlay evidence.
manualStatus: measured; one machine, one core count, server-level only
